correctness.rationale: For positive injective compact A in S_p and 0<p<1, the fractional-power integral gives a positive resolvent-difference trace formula; rank-one addition stays in S_p. Sherman–Morrison gives the trace integrand t s^p⟨v,(A+sI)^(−2)v⟩/(1+t⟨v,(A+sI)^(−1)v⟩), times sin(pi p)/pi. After division by t, monotone convergence and the scalar beta integral give p times the inverse-power quadratic form, possibly infinite for the positive branch alone. If v=A^(1/2)w is a unit vector, P_v≤||w||²A makes A−tP_v nonnegative for t small enough, so Loewner–Heinz selects the plus branch. On this range the derivative is finite by the spectral theorem. The p-power trace quasi-triangle inequality gives the same baseline trace at t=0 from equal profiles. Two-sided comparability gives equality of square-root ranges by the operator range criterion. Loewner–Heinz and inverse order (obtainable by shifted inverses and monotone form limits) give equivalent form norms for A^(p−1) and B^(p−1). Eigenvalue truncation for A makes their common square-root range a core in either form norm. Equality of responses on normalized core vectors, then homogeneity and polarization, identifies the closed forms and therefore the operators by spectral calculus. The branch threshold may depend on v; uniformity in v is not needed. The extension of the plus-branch derivative by itself does not establish behavior of the max outside the stated range. The frozen finite checker was read, not run, and its reported 1,332 checks are not evidence of common-core completeness.
